entry_state: Scenario redistribution conserves mass but changes the target distribution. Output error needs regularity; policy regret needs uniform comparison over a shared feasible information-based class. Threshold bounds require control near the boundary, and temporal transport requires adapted information. The repaired finite coupling supplies explicit initial and common-loss premises; feedback can amplify local errors.
exit_state: Approximation must retain its exact, bounded and sampled contributions and use stopping rules matched to the question. Decisions require an explicit objective and admissible policy class. Worst-case, regret and multiple-prior objectives differ; stagewise pasting can change a fixed hidden contract into a switching adversary, so commitment and reoptimization must remain explicit.
